newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: FOCUS - Czech unions extend national rail strike.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Czech unions extend national rail strike.

text.p: Czech railway unions on Friday voted to extend a national rail strike, already in its fourth day, for another 24 hours, the Czech news agency CTK reported, quoting the executive secretary of the unions' leadership.
Mojmir Bakalar of the Association of Unions of Railway Workers (OSZ) told CTK that the strike would run through at least midnight on Saturday.
But Transport Minister Martin Riman said his talks with OSZ leaders would continue on Friday, and that there was still a chance to find a compromise.
"I think that we have a chance (to conclude the strike)," Riman told reporters after emerging from talks at the government central office.
It was not clear if Riman had been informed yet of the unions' decision taken in another part of Prague.
The action, which began Tuesday and was originally planned as a 48-hour stoppage, was extended to a fourth day on Friday after both unions and the government dug in their heels.
The OSZ is demanding the removal of the state railway's management and a rethink of plans to reform the rail system which could cost tens of thousands of jobs if implemented.
Union and government officials were hopeful that the strike could be ended on Friday through a meeting of the tripartite council which combines union, industry, and government leaders.
A Prague court has ruled that the strike is illegal, but Riman has said that striking workers would not be fired if they would return to work quickly.

The strike is the first major confrontation between organised labour and the government since the fall of communism in 1989, and the industrial action may begin to get support from other labour unions.
CTK quoted leaders of unions representing electrical workers as saying that they were considering a sympathy strike if an agreement with the railway workers was not soon reached.
Businesses are warning the shutdown in freight service will seriously bite into earnings if the strike gets drawn out.
Cities have added buses to relieve commmuter pressure, but international trains have been halted at borders with Germany, Poland, Austria, and Slovakia.
